MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  Special City Council Meeting

  June 16, 2022

A Special Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Bucknum at 6:01p.m., on June 16, 2022, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on June 15, 2022, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also posted
at Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and Norman P. Murray
Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Goodell (via teleconference)
  Council Member Kelley
  Council Member Raths
  Mayor Pro Tem Sachs
  Mayor Bucknum

Absent:  None

Staff Present: Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk

INVOCATION: Council Member Raths

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Kelley

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: Commented that the Judge in yesterdays hearing seemed to be unaware of
the many circumstances surrounding the lawsuit. Ms. Schlicht asked if the City Attorney
suppressed material facts from the court and if so, was the court mislead and thereby this Stipulated
Judgement was weaponized against the public. She stated that the City lost its opposition in the
ex-parte hearing and the lawsuits have been transferred back to the Judge Shwarm with the hearing
scheduled for June 28.

City Council Special Meeting Minutes  1  June 16, 2022
 City Attorney clarified that Judge Gastelum in department 11 had all the documents and cases. He
transferred it and was received yesterday by Judge Shwarm. Judge Shwarm noted that he had not
seen the papers and had no idea what was in them since he just received them. City Attorney said
there was no misinformation or who knew what because the courts have had all the information
since 2018.

Carlos Pianelli, M.V.: Expressed that or children are the most important asset and our schools are
the most important real estate. He spoke out about school safety and laid out facts on gun violence
throughout our Country. Stressed that we need a security system to protect the children and offered
his assistance to the City Council.

City Manager Wilberg announced that on June 1 he received a call from the broker of the property
owners that own the CVS building. The broker indicated that the property is on the market and
wanted to know if there was any city interest. Mr. Wilberg indicated to the broker that the City is
interested, but as the City Manager he does not have the authority to commit the City one way or
the other until discussed by the City Council which would give staff direction. He stated that we
are hear this evening to discuss the fact that the CVS store is for sale not CVS itself. The things to
consider first is the project proposal could stop before it even gets started. That being said, if there
is interest in looking at the opportunity further, there are a number of things we would look into as
part of our due diligence. Some of which are included in the brief staff report, such as the sale and
offer price, financing, funding mechanisms, and any third-party participation opportunities so that
the City would not have to use any funds. He stated that since this past Tuesday when this
opportunity was announced he has received three different calls that there are some third parties
interested which would be very interested in partnering with the City. He said there would be the
normal review of the building itself and the structural integrity and hazmat issues. All these things
would need to be looked at before there would be any kind of recommended by staff back to the
City Council or for any opportunity for the City Council to decide. Lastly, he emphasized this
evening that we are not buying a property, we are not spending any money, and that he is just
bringing forth the information that the property is for sale and is there any interest on the part of
the City becoming involved.

OPEN SESSION

  Discussion considering the purchase by the City, or in some form of
  collaboration with other parties, of the Real Property in the Village Center
  upon which the CVS Store is located 25272 Marguerite Parkway, Mission
  Viejo, CA 92692. The property owner is offering the Core Area property for
  sale on the open market to the general public. The seller has directly invited
  the City to make an offer to purchase the Real Property upon which the CVS
  store operates. The City Council will deliberate, after receipt of public and
  staff testimony.

  The City Manager Dennis Wilberg, Assistant City Manager Keith Rattay, and
  City Attorney William Curley gave the report.

  Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: Stated that an election year brings out transparency compared to
  purchase of the Stein Mart property. She recapped the history of the Stein Mart agenda
  items. She questioned if Mr. Breton was apprised ahead of time of this walk-on item at

City Council Special Meeting Minutes  2  June 16, 2022
   last Tuesday’s City Council Meeting. She asked what the City has planned for the Stein
  Mart and that there are bond payments being made with no return on investment.

  Carlos Pianelli, M.V.: Stated that the residents are angry with the process and felt the
  City was pressured and pointed out that not many residents knew about this meeting.
  Asked about the Core Area Vision Plan and how long is it going to take.

  Tom Moore, M.V.: Commented on the specific plan and stressed that it’s important for
  the community to understand what is going into the Core Area.

  Cathy Palmer, M.V.: Voiced her concerns on the purchase of the CVS building and feels
  that the decision is being rushed and the input the public provides is not taken seriously.
  She stated real estate purchases by cities that there is potential for conflicts of interest and
  undue influence with developers. She is in favor of a private entity but not in favor of
  putting the residents on the hook for more real estate development. Urged the Council to
  move cautiously.

  Gideon Victor, M.V.: Spoke in favor of mixed-use housing. Outlined the debt ratio of the
  City if they were to purchase this property.

  Robert Breton, M.V.: Clarified that the allegation that he knew about the walk-on item at
  the last Council Meeting was incorrect. He was at City Hall to discuss business with the
  City Manager. Stated that this city is master planned, it is beautiful by design due to the
  visionary leadership and hard work of the city council and city staff. Emphasized that the
  City needs to explore this valuable opportunity.

  Wendy Lee, M.V.: Expressed concerns about the economy. She feels these funds should
  be kept in reserves and not spent. Questioned if the City would have to buy out the lease
  of CVS or not build for the eight years that are left on the CVS lease. She is in favor of
  developing the shopping center but to take into consideration the current economy.

  The Council Member’s asked various questions.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Sachs to receive input from the Investment Advisory
  Commission as expeditiously as possible.

  Motion failed for lack of second.

  Motion made by Council Member Goodell to move this item to Closed Session to discuss
  taking the steps recommended by staff in terms of exploring the opportunity of price and
  terms to start the process.

  Council Member Goodell amended his motion to authorize staff to contact the owner of
  this property and enter into discussions about the terms that would be necessary before
  spending money on the due diligence items.

  Motion failed for lack of second.

City Council Special Meeting Minutes  3  June 16, 2022
   Motion made Council Member Goodell to direct staff reach out to the seller and depending
  on how that is received we will look at the expenditures and due diligence.

  Motion failed for lack of second.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Sachs, seconded by Mayor Bucknum to direct staff not
  to move forward on the purchase of this property.

  Council Member Goodell asked for a substitute motion to direct the City
  Manager to incorporate the finance and administration committee into the
  process to evaluate any financing terms and to explore private party
  partnerships where the city would not have to spend any money in this process
  and to reach out and talk to the owners to put together a deal under those
  conditions.

  Motion failed for lack of second

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Sachs, seconded by Mayor Bucknum to direct staff not
  to move forward on the purchase of this property.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  Goodell
  ABSENT: None

  City Attorney stated that a Closed Session will not be rendered.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 7:20 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this special
meeting, Mayor Bucknum adjourned the meeting

______________________________________________
Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of June 28, 2022
